Send
Connect on a trusted local network

Open RedrainCast on both devices. Nearby receivers update automatically. Choose Send, or enter the IP and current TCP port shown by the receiver.

Receiving starts automatically while this app is open. It pauses before Android screen-sharing consent and resumes after sending stops, fails, or is cancelled. Only one cast is active at a time.

Incoming video fills the screen without an in-app overlay. Use Stop on the sender to end the cast and return the receiver to its home screen. Android Back/Home still lets you leave the app, which closes its receiver; sending can continue through its foreground service.

When both peers support stream recovery, brief backlog stalls discard an obsolete dependency chain and resume at a fresh keyframe, keeping the session alive. The same codec, requested quality and bounded buffers are retained. Peers without that capability keep strict congestion errors. Failed decoders, broken connections or recovery timeouts still report errors.

The receiver uses an OS-assigned TCP port, which may change when listening restarts. UDP 27183 discovers receivers. Use only a trusted LAN; the connection is not encrypted.

Android requires your screen-sharing approval. Source apps may block playback-audio capture. No codec, quality or audio fallback is applied.
